To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GNNs can be trained incrementally and that a window of size one is sufficient to achieve good performance.

(1) the receptive field size of GNNs is not a bottleneck, (2) the receptive field can be permanently deleted after a few time steps, and (3) GNNs can be trained incrementally over a temporal window of only one time step.
(i) GNNs can be trained incrementally over a small window and (ii) the performance of GNNs can even improve by deleting data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: when can data be permanently deleted in online learning of GNNs?
the question of how much of the training data is necessary to retain the GNNs performance, and how to delete the data permanently, when the training data is growing and changing over time.
how much data is necessary to retain a certain performance when learning on temporal graphs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data can be deleted permanently, as soon as the model is trained.
, in general, the performance of GNNs can be maintained when deleting old data.
the GNNs we tested are very robust to the deletion of old training data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GNNs can be trained over a sliding window of temporal graphs and can retain a good performance, even when only a small fraction of the graph's history is considered.
we can train GNNs on a temporal window of a few months, which is much less than the full graph, and still retain a good performance.
the GNNs we experimented with are able to adapt to new data and that they do not need to be trained over a large amount of data to retain a good performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GNNs' receptive field is the key to understanding when data can be safely deleted.
GNNs can be incrementally trained and evaluated on evolving temporal graphs, without the need to retrain over the complete graph.
, in many cases, it is sufficient to train GNNs over small windows of data, which allows for permanent data deletion.
